acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria

The deliverables are considered “accepted” when they meet the following criteria.

  1. A research paper that includes: literature review, market analysis, competitor analysis, stakeholder interviews
  2. Literature Review: The literature review should be thorough and include proper citation.
  3. Market Analysis: This should cover macro-level information explaining why seed phrase-based wallet recovery hinders mass adoption. It should also analyze the need for a no-code SSI platform to achieve mass adoption.
  4. Competitor Analysis: This should examine organizations currently offering wallets without seed phrase management, along with other no-code SSI platforms.
  5. Stakeholder Interviews: The records should include names (or initials), interview dates, recordings or transcripts, and reasons for selection.
  6. Research Paper Drafting: The paper should include all the above-mentioned elements and be saved on Notion with a publicly accessible link.
  7. A video walkthrough of the research paper should clearly demonstrate how the aforementioned acceptance criteria have been fulfilled.
description:
Milestone 1: Market and Technical Research

Outputs

Milestone 1 has the following outputs (deliverables):

  1. A research paper that includes: literature review, market analysis, competitor analysis, and stakeholder interviews.
  2. A video walk through of the research paper

In order to deliver the aforementioned deliverable, we will conduct the following activities.

  1. Literature Review: Review existing literature for understanding.
  2. Market Analysis: Evaluate demand and identify market gaps.
  3. Competitor Analysis: Assess similar offerings from competitors to pinpoint differentiators and opportunities.
  4. Stakeholder Interviews: Interview key stakeholders and record their insights, including interview dates. Include their names, roles, and reasons for selection.
  5. Research Paper Drafting: Summarize the findings from the above activities in a comprehensive research paper.
  6. Video Walkthrough: Create a filmed walkthrough.
title: Market and Technical Research

  2. SSI Platform v1.0 Figma Design File - First iteration: The design should have essential user stories for issuing verifiable credentials. For example:
  • As a business, I can carry out the Know Your Customer (KYC) process.
  • As a business, I can issue work certificates.

The prototype on Figma will include interactions that reviewers can click on to view how the app behaves. The design should include the following user stories:
  • As a business, I can confirm that the user has completed the proper Know Your Customer (KYC) process.
  • As a business, I can authenticate the user's work certificate.
  • As a business, I can authenticate the user's educational certificate.
  • As a business, I can use zero-knowledge proofs to verify that the user is at least 18 years old.
  1. SSI Platform v3.0 Production-ready design in Figma. The design will include the following user stories:
  • As a business, I can carry out the Know Your Customer (KYC) process.
  • As a business, I can issue work certificates.
  • As a business, I can issue educational certificates.

  • As a business, I can authenticate the user's work certificate.

“Production-ready” means that it doesn’t need more work from designers and is ready for the engineering team to turn the design into code.

description:
Bring’s wallet-side application comprising of:

  • Chrome extension code for the partner wallet 
  • All UIs 
  • Tokens cache for ADA 
  • Backend support for all the above (APIs)
  • Functionalities of Chrome extension:

Popup part:

Get a domain list from our API, cache it locally, and update the domain list every 48 hours.

Check every domain that the user goes to if the domain is included in the domain list.

Integrate with the extension and get the relevant wallet address.

Open a popup that offers cashback for relevant domains.

Opt-out - turn off popups for various time frames.

Activate a deal - Register the deal using the specific wallet address.

Redirect to the relevant URL for the deal.

Check if the user has any new rewards and open a popup with details about the update and where he can see more details.

Custom themes - allowing the outlets that are using our extension to customize the theme of the popup.

Retailers part:

Display a list of all retailers available and relevant to the user’s country.

Have the ability to filter the retailer's list by category or by search.

Activate a deal for a specific retailer and get cashback for this purchase.

Show the total tokens the user gained by buying at our retailers.

Show detailed information about previous purchases and claims.

Claim the eligible tokens to the user’s wallet.


  • UI break down:

Earn crypto cashback popup (showing the wallet address it’s connected to)

Turn off functionality (choosing time period for stop getting offers)

Cashback terms & conditions for approval

New cashback reward notification (to notify users they can earn it / claim it)

Claim Cashback

Cashback History

Cashback offers + search bar and categories

Rewards feed where the user can review all earned rewards


  • Functionality of the tokens cache
  • The APIs that will be developed:

Popup part:

/domains - Get the list of relevant domains

/validate-domain - validate that specific domain is still relevant for cashback.

/check-events - Check if the user has an update about his cache.

/activate - Activate a new deal for the user

Retailers part:

/activate - Activate a new deal for the user.

/cache - Get information about the user’s cache.

/check-availability - Check if the service is available for the user’s country.

/retailers - Get the list of retailers available for the user’s country.

/categories-search - Get the categories and search terms available for filtering the retailer’s list.

/claim-init - Initiate the claim process for claiming eligible tokens, the user will have the ability to choose the amount to claim.

/claim-submit - Submit the claim process and move the tokens to the user’s wallet.


  • Detailed documentation (Chrome extension code, UIs, tokens cache, and APIs)
  • User manuals for testing
title: Building the ADA Cashback

description:
We will use a framework designed to help developers build applications that combine large language models (LLMs) with other sources of computation or knowledge. ​​It allows efficient integration of different LLMs, which can help compare models and choose the best one for a specific use case. Additionally,  the framework is designed to manage complex workflows and interactions between LLMs and external tools or databases, which is beneficial for implementing data collection, analysis, and feedback integration.

LLM that will be considered include:


•  OpenAI’s GPT-4: Suitable for natural language understanding and generation tasks.

•  Anthropic’s Claude: Known for safe and aligned language model outputs.

•  Cohere’s Command R: Designed for retrieval-augmented generation tasks.

•  Local Models (like LLaMA, Falcon, etc.): These can be deployed locally to have more control over data privacy and customization.


We should make a comparison between at least 3 AI models based on the following benchmarking for acceptance:

• Accuracy: How well the model summarizes, evaluates, and analyzes proposals without losing essential details.

• Response Time: How fast the model processes tasks.

• Alignment with Community Needs: Does the model’s output meet the specific requirements of the Cardano community?

• Cost Efficiency: What are the costs associated with running and fine-tuning the model?

• Customization: How easily can the model be fine-tuned or adapted to specific governance needs?

We will also collect data to configure the agent to have the correct knowledge base. The data include:

•  Cardano Constitution: To ensure the AI Assistant operates within the legal framework.

•  Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIPs): Past and present proposals to understand the scope and nature of governance issues.

•  Community Discussions: Forum discussions, social media conversations, and other channels where the Cardano community debates proposals and governance.

•  Historical Data (if available): Past voting records, dRep decisions, and data on the impact of implemented proposals to provide context for future decision-making.


To properly fine-tune the LLM, we must initially collect at least 1-2 GB. This data would be structured as follows:

• Text Data (Proposals, Constitutions): Provide text files or documents formatted consistently.

• Metadata: Details like the proposal date, authors and voting outcomes.

• Feedback and Discussions: Organize by source (forums, surveys, social media) and tag them with sentiments if necessary for the LLM training.

• Training Data: Split data into training, validation, and testing sets.
title: Choose LLM Model to use, collect data

acceptance_criteria:
AI agent can successfully complete at least one task in a controlled environment.

To evaluate the outputs, we consider the following measurable KPIs:

• Accuracy: How accurately the AI performs tasks, such as summarizing or evaluating proposals (target above 85%).

• Response Time: Time it takes the AI agent to complete a task (e.g., less than 7 seconds per task).

• Error Rate: Percentage of outputs that require manual correction (should aim for <10%).


 The LLM’s response should:

• Be concise and accurate.

• Provide clear, actionable insights for decision-making (e.g., feasibility analysis, budget assessment).

• Align with governance principles, Cardano constitution and community needs.

• Be generated within a reasonable timeframe (e.g., under 7 seconds).

  3. The wallet address for verification will be shared along with the URL.
  4. Confirm that the transaction can be retrieved on the transaction management screen.
  5. Check the ADA balance on the dashboard and confirm that it matches the actual token amount.

Note:

Q. How can transactions be verified?

A. Register the mainnet wallet address in the app and compare its output results with Cardanoscan (https://cardanoscan.io/). We will provide wallet addresses that already contain transactions. The target wallet addresses will be shared along with the development environment URL at the time of milestone submission. The reason for not sharing the wallet at this point is to reduce the verification burden. The intention is to prevent spam from being sent and burying the transactions we actually want to test within the next 3 months.

  • Gas fees → Generated along with the sent transaction
  • Fund transfers → The app recognizes transfers from registered walletA to walletB. For this verification, we will prepare two wallet addresses.
  • Swaps → We will use Minswap, Muesliswap, etc. We can't be definitive here because there's a possibility that the DEX might be down at the time of verification.
  • transfer and deposit of native tokens → Generated along with the sent transaction.
  • Staking rewards → Rewards received for each epoch. These will also be included in the prepared wallet.
  • NFT transfer → Transactions for sending or receiving NFTs. We will also share wallet addresses that include the target verification for this.

Q. Will the testing be done on the testnet?

A. It will be on the mainnet.

description:
• Midgard outbox smart contract
  • Midgard inbox smart contract

The checkpoint mechanism evolved greatly to inherit more security from the Cardano L1 then what was possible in the original milestone

The event inbox is the set of events received from the L1 blockchain by the Midgard L2.

The block producer will receive a list of events from the L1 by some relayer, and then include the merkle root of the events in the block header.

There are two types of events that can be received from the L1:

Messages - these contain arbitrary information sent from Cardano L1 to the Midgard L2. This information can be used to move assets from Cardano to Midgard or to communicate other information about events on Cardano to Midgard. 

Transactions - These are transactions that are submitted on the Cardano L1 that must be executed in the Midgard L2. This "Forced Transaction Inclusion" is a security feature that allows participants of the Midgard network to access their funds in the (unlikely) event that Midgard block production is compromised or malicious, e.g. the block producer is censoring transactions. This is one of the powerful mechanisms through which Midgard inherits Cardano's security.

The Midgard event outbox is the set of messages sent to the L1 blockchain from the Midgard blockchain and acts similarly to the event inbox except in the other direction (from Midgard to Cardano).
title: Midgard outbox and inbox smart contracts

  • The implementation passes all unit tests designed to verify the correctness and completeness of the basic builtin functions.

Library of Theorems for Proving Smart Contract Security

  • A comprehensive library of theorems is developed to assist in proving the security of Coq-Plutus smart contracts against common vulnerabilities.
  • The library includes specific theorems for detecting and preventing the following vulnerabilities:
  • Double Satisfaction: Theorems that ensure no double satisfaction can occur in any transaction scenario.
  • Unbounded Datum: Theorems that prevent the usage of unbounded datum values, ensuring data size limits are enforced.
  • Unbounded Value: Theorems that enforce constraints on the values used in smart contracts, preventing unbounded value issues.
  • Staking Control Theft: Theorems that secure staking controls, ensuring that unauthorized parties cannot steal staking control.
  • Other Token Name Minting Attack: Theorems that prevent the unauthorized minting of tokens with names that could lead to attacks.

description:

  1. ADA Payment Option: The WooCommerce plugin (internal name: ADA-Plugin) introduces a new payment method within the WooCommerce checkout, allowing customers to select ADA as their preferred payment option.
  2. Exchange Rate Calculation: The WooCommerce plugin dynamically calculates the ADA amount required for the transaction, based on the current exchange rate between the shop’s base currency (USD, EUR) and ADA.

title: Payment Module for WooCommerce

2. Transaction Signing: The user can sign the Bitcoin transaction using their private key and receive a confirmation that the transaction is signed and ready to be sent.

3. Transaction broadcasting: The user can broadcast the signed Bitcoin transaction to the Bitcoin network and includes a fee for the transaction confirmation by miners.
description:
Enhance the wallet’s functionality to support Bitcoin transactions in addition to ADA, utilizing their similar UTXO transaction models. The milestone outputs are specific functionalities to be implemented in the Begin Wallet (Chrome) include:

1. Transaction Creation: The Begin Wallet enables users to assemble a Bitcoin transaction by selecting appropriate UTXOs (Unspent Transaction Outputs), defining the recipient's address and the amount to be sent, and automatically calculating the necessary transaction fees based on current network conditions.

2. Transaction Signing: The wallet securely signs the assembled Bitcoin transaction using the user's private key, ensuring that only the rightful owner can authorize the transfer of Bitcoin, thereby maintaining transaction integrity and security.

3. Transaction Broadcasting: Once signed, the wallet broadcasts the Bitcoin transaction to the Bitcoin network, ensuring it is propagated across the network nodes for validation. The transaction includes a calculated fee to incentivize miners to confirm and include the transaction in a new block, finalizing the transfer.
title: Bitcoin Compatibility

3. QR Code scanning: Scan a QR code displayed on a desktop monitor with their smartphone, containing the merchant’s wallet address and the exact ADA amount to be paid.

4. Checkout display payment: Complete the payment using their ADA wallet within the checkout process.

Clarification: The WooCommerce plugin is used in beta-test phase, meaning it is being used prior to official approval by WooCommerce.

Milestone 4: Bitcoin Compatibility

The milestones are considered successfully achieved if a user of the Begin Wallet (Chrome) can:

1. Transaction Creation: The user can assemble a Bitcoin transaction by entering the recipient's Bitcoin address, specifying the amount of Bitcoin to be sent, and seeing the transaction fee calculated based on the current network conditions.

2. Transaction Signing: The user can sign the Bitcoin transaction using their private key and receive a confirmation that the transaction is signed and ready to be sent.

3. Transaction broadcasting: The user can broadcast the signed Bitcoin transaction to the Bitcoin network and includes a fee for the transaction confirmation by miners.

description:
Launch all functionalities from the milestone outputs to be implemented in the Begin Wallet (Chrome) or via partners or on WooCommerce on live / production (no test-environment).

Final close-out Report and Final closeout Video for:

Milestone 1: Voting Integration

1. User Registration System for Voting: A system that allows users to register as eligible voters, ensuring they meet the necessary criteria and can participate in voting activities.

2. Voting: An interface in the frontend of Begin App where users can cast their votes on various items, ensuring recording of each vote on the blockchain.

3. Voting Results Display: A display of voting results, providing users with information on voting outcomes.

Milestone 2: Biometric Seedphrase

1. Biometric Enrollment: Biometric Data Capture in reference to ISO/IEC 19794-5 or similar standards for capturing facial image data.

2. Seedphrase Derivation: Develop an algorithm to convert biometric data into a seedphrase.

3. Authentication System: Login to the Begin Wallet (Chrome) utilizing the generated seedphrase and facial recognition to support passwordless authentication.

4. Authorization System: Transaction Authorization: Develop an authorization mechanism where users can authorize transactions using their biometric data and seedphrase.

Milestone 3: Payment Module for WooCommerce


1. ADA Payment Option: The WooCommerce plugin (internal name: ADA-Plugin) introduces a new payment method within the WooCommerce checkout, allowing customers to select ADA as their preferred payment option.

2. Exchange Rate Calculation: The WooCommerce plugin dynamically calculates the ADA amount required for the transaction, based on the current exchange rate between the shop’s base currency (USD, EUR) and ADA.

3. QR Code Generation: Upon selecting ADA as the payment method, the plugin generates a QR code containing the merchant’s wallet address and the exact ADA amount to be paid by the customer.

4. Checkout Display: The QR code is displayed during the checkout process, enabling the customer to scan it with their ADA-compatible wallet app to initiate the payment.

Milestone 4: Bitcoin Compatibility

1. Transaction Creation: The Begin Wallet enables users to assemble a Bitcoin transaction by selecting appropriate UTXOs (Unspent Transaction Outputs), defining the recipient's address and the amount to be sent, and automatically calculating the necessary transaction fees based on current network conditions.

2. Transaction Signing: The wallet securely signs the assembled Bitcoin transaction using the user's private key, ensuring that only the rightful owner can authorize the transfer of Bitcoin, thereby maintaining transaction integrity and security.

3. Transaction Broadcasting: Once signed, the wallet broadcasts the Bitcoin transaction to the Bitcoin network, ensuring it is propagated across the network nodes for validation. The transaction includes a calculated fee to incentivize miners to confirm and include the transaction in a new block, finalizing the transfer.

description:
1. Specification document for on-chain validators and minting policies.
  2. Specification document for the auxiliary deterministic algorithms.
  3. Specification document for the async messaging protocol.
  4. Specification document for the architecture of Hydrozoa components.
  5. Open-source project repository and project board populated with expected Milestone 2 tasks/issues.

Response to Reviewer 1’s comments on 2024-08-13:

Tentative TOC for on-chain validators and minting policies:

  • Hydrozoa head minting policy
  • Hydrozoa head state validator
  • Hydrozoa deposit validator
  • Hydrozoa contestation mechanism validator

Tentative TOC for auxiliary deterministic algorithms:

  • AlgoSettle – deterministic algorithm to construct a tree of settlement transactions
  • AlgoDissolveCert – deterministic algorithm to construct a tree of dissolution certificates
  • AlgoDissolveTx – deterministic algorithm to construct a tree of dissolution transactions from a tree of dissolution certificates and halted head state.

Tentative TOC for async messaging protocol between L2 participants:

  • ReqTx – request a transaction to be included in the next snapshot
  • ReqDep – request a multi-signed assurance transaction to facilitate a deposit from L1
  • ReqWdr – request a subset of the L2 utxo set to be withdrawn in the next snapshot
  • ReqSn – request signatures from the L2 participants for a snapshot
  • AckSn – acknowledge a snapshot with a signature
  • ReqFn – request a final snapshot from the snapshot leader

Tentative TOC for Hydrozoa architecture:

  • Processes and components (Cardano node, hydrozoa node, wallet, etc.)
  • Codebase architecture (repositories, packages, modules)
  • On-chain script interdependencies

Note that the above TOCs are subject to change during the course of the project as the Hydrozoa design is refined based on feedback from implementation.

acceptance_criteria:
1. Detailed Project Plan:

The research report should cover all relevant aspects of Cardano’s blockchain and smart contract functionalities, clearly understanding their capabilities. The applicable elements to be covered include:

  • Scalability: Analysis of Cardano’s ability to handle increased transaction volumes.
  • Security: Assessment of security features and potential vulnerabilities.
  • Smart Contract Functionality: Detailed overview of the capabilities and limitations of Cardano’s smart contracts.
  • Cost Efficiency: Comparison of transaction costs and other operational expenses with current blockchain solutions.
  • Ecosystem and Community Support: Insight into the development community, existing projects, and overall ecosystem support for Cardano.

2. Expansion Strategy Approval:

The expansion strategy must be thorough and feasible, to ensure clarity and measurability:

  • Thoroughness: The strategy document should include:
  • Step-by-Step Expansion Plan: Detailed phases including preparation, execution, and post-expansion activities.
  • Risk Assessment and Mitigation Plan: Identification of potential risks and the corresponding mitigation strategies.
  • Feasibility:
  • Technical Feasibility: Evaluation of technical requirements and the ability to meet them within the current infrastructure.
  • Operational Feasibility: Assessment of the operational impact and readiness of the organization for expansion.

3. Approval from Key Stakeholders and Advisors:

Secure formal approval from key stakeholders and advisors through a review meeting, documented with meeting minutes or a signed agreement.

description:
• Create private/local website in preparation of launching a public proof of concept in milestone 4 (live website)
  • Front-end user interface to view coupon codes that have been posted on-chain
  • Coupon codes (e.g. online retailer codes are listed that are validated recently so users don't have to search retailmenot.com and other sources to check if it is validated)
  • Proof of concept validation of coupon codes using Charli3 Oracles;
  • (Required) POC Integration with Charli3 Oracles:
  • Problem: Coupon codes expire and users search through multiple sites to find valid codes
  • Solution: Charli3 Oracles nodes check and validate the status of coupons and post that data on-chain to be consumed by the front-end
  • Architectural flow (proposed and may change): Charli3 is working with Veralidity to integrate data directly into Magento, then Magento places data on-chain, and then this validation step has a node or node network from Charli3 validate in real-time the status of a coupon code to ensure it is still active
  • MVP for this project: Single node network real-time validation of coupon to demonstrate capabilities
  • Enhancement (Optional deliverable if possible): multi-node network with consensus mechanism (we leave this as optional as this is a POC project and may be beyond the scope of what we can deliver, this is aligned with the original proposal)
  • (Required) Validation that a coupon is active displayed on website including time the status was last checked
  • (Optional) Additional information obtained during the Charli3 Oracles real-time update
title: Create local/private website showing the coupon codes/NFT data and includes basic validation info

Acceptance Criteria

The deliverables will be considered "approved" if the following criteria are met:

1.Backend Development

・The backend code is published on GitHub.

・Documentation explaining the backend development process is provided.

 This includes the following requirement 

【Off-chain token transactions】

Sending and receiving tokens between users

 ・Users send and receive tokens to and from other users via the off-chain platform.

・Real-time Processing

Transactions are processed in real-time on the off-chain platform, and balances between users are updated immediately.

 

2.Blockchain Development

・The blockchain component code is published on GitHub.

・Documentation explaining the blockchain development process is provided.

This includes the following requirement

【Transaction Aggregation and On-Chain Commit】

・Daily Batch Processing

At a fixed time each day, all transactions that have occurred off-chain are aggregated.

A Merkle tree is constructed from the aggregated transactions, and the Merkle root (root hash) is calculated.

・ On-chain commitment of the Merkle root

The calculated Merkle root is committed to a smart contract on the Cardano blockchain.

This process records the day's transactions on the blockchain, ensuring the integrity of the entire system.

【User Verification of Transactions】

・Weekly Verification

Once a week, users verify that their transactions have been correctly reflected on-chain.

To do this, they use the corresponding Merkle proof and check it against the Merkle root on the smart contract.

・Provision of verification tools

In order to make it easier for users to verify transactions, we will provide a web interface and dedicated tools to create an environment where users can easily verify transactions.

3.Unit Testing

The unit test code is published on GitHub.

The unit test results, conducted by in-house developers, are compiled in a report.

4.Manual Testing

The results of the manual testing are compiled in a report.

The procedures and results of the manual tests, conducted by in-house developers, are detailed.

5.Bug Fixes

The fixed bug code is published on GitHub.

Documentation explaining the bug fixes is provided.

6.NEO88 DAO (Voting phaze to determine Overall plan within this DAO)

・Based on the discussions at the previous milestone, the fundamental issues of NEO88DAO will be decided by vote.

And this vote will be held by at least 30% DAO members.

The DAO members will vote on the following issues.

・The main focus will be on creating events to boost Shikoku, but other objectives

・Prioritising what the DAO will do

・The authority and role of each member

・Token design, etc.

・The result of the voting is shared with Community.

 As a premise,

we will use a custodial wallet to onboard the general public who are not familiar with Web3 this time.

However, the tokens that will be exchanged this time are tokens that will only be used for activities within the region, and are not the kind that will be sold on the market and have a huge monetary value.

In addition, since we will be managing assets with this wallet (we will not be putting other cryptocurrencies, etc. into this wallet), we believe that custodial management will be fine.

The reason for using a system where the tokens of the app users are transacted off-chain, and the data of these transactions is recorded on-chain on

【Problems that arise when implementing tokens transaction completely on-chain】

1. Because each user has to create their own transaction, ADA is required.

This is too difficult for the target users of this app (who have never even touched blockchain before. And it cannot be said that Web3 tools are easy to use for everyone.).

This is the main reason.

2. This token does not have any asset value, so to be honest, there is not that much value in strictly preventing tampering on-chain.

3. Since it is often exchanged in real-life situations, real-time performance is important. (It is necessary to shorten the time taken for transactions.)

【Reasons for putting the daily transactions on-chain】

1. In the case that a user suspects tampering, they should be able to verify it themselves

2. In the future, when literacy in the region increases and the environment is set up so that ADA is easily accessible to the general public, when all of this token's transactions are carried out on-chain, it should be possible to show that　“on-chain data” is being referenced.

  • Successful integration and data collection from at least three different IoT devices.
  • Quantifiable metric: Protocol operational with three different IoT devices, with detailed integration plans documented.

Refinement of Decentralized Storage Mechanism:

  • A mechanism for storing data in an open and decentralized manner must be implemented. Data collected from at least three IoT devices must be stored in a decentralized manner, with functional integrations to existing storage providers.
  • Quantifiable metric: Decentralised storage mechanism documented and operational with no critical issues remaining.

Field Testing of the Solution:

  • Field testing must be successfully completed, including the collection of clear and verifiable data from at least three different IoT devices. The system must allow for the successful collection and verification of this data.
  • Quantifiable metric: Field test results showing at least 95% data integrity and accuracy.

Documentation of Issues Encountered and Solutions Implemented:

  • All critical issues identified during field testing and/or related to decentralized storage mechanisms must be resolved. Clear documentation, written in English and in PDF format, must be provided. This documentation must be publicly available on GitHub and understandable to both technical and non-technical people.
  • Quantifiable metric: Detailed documentation available in PDF format, written in English.

Detailed Plans of How zK Can Be Implemented:

  • A complete zK implementation plan must be developed, covering 100% of the components required for the integration. This plan must be documented in a PDF written in English and made available on GitHub.
  • Quantifiable metric: zK implementation plans documented in a PDF, written in English.

Documentation for the Prototype Available: Comprehensive documentation should be available, detailing the prototype's features, setup instructions, and usage guidelines.

description:
Develop the Initial Prototype of the DevX Wallet: Create the first working version of the DevX Wallet, focusing on implementing the foundational architecture and core functionalities.

Implement Core Features: Integrate the following essential features into the prototype:

  • Advanced User Wallet Debugging: Tools and interfaces that allow users to debug their wallets effectively.
  • Quick Wallet Creation: A streamlined process for users to create new wallets efficiently.
  • Keyphrase Exporting: Secure mechanisms for users to export their keyphrases.
  • Detailed Transaction Overviews: Comprehensive views and histories of all transactions.
  • Listing Detailed Wallet UTXOs: Detailed listings and management of Unspent Transaction Outputs (UTXOs) for each wallet.

Conduct Initial Internal Testing: Perform thorough internal testing of the prototype to identify and fix major bugs, ensuring that the core functionalities work as intended.

Prepare Documentation for the Prototype: Develop detailed documentation that explains the prototype’s features, functionalities, and usage guidelines.
title: Prototype Development and Initial Testing

acceptance_criteria:
Pilot Phase Successfully Launched: The pilot phase must be officially initiated, with the selected group of users actively using the DevX Wallet.

Feedback Collected from Pilot Users: Detailed feedback should be collected from all pilot participants, providing insights into their experiences and suggestions for improvement.

Support and Training Provided to Pilot Users: Pilot users must receive adequate support and training to ensure they can use the wallet effectively and provide meaningful feedback.

List of Prioritized Enhancements and Bug Fixes Based on Feedback: A documented list of feature enhancements and bug fixes, prioritized based on the collected feedback, should be created to inform future development efforts.
description:
Launch a Pilot Phase with a Select Group of Developers and Support Personnel: Initiate the pilot phase by engaging a select group of developers and support personnel who will use and evaluate the DevX Wallet prototype. This phase is critical for gathering real-world usage data and identifying any practical issues.

Collect Detailed User Feedback and Identify Areas for Improvement: Implement a systematic approach to collect detailed feedback from pilot users. This feedback will focus on user experience, feature functionality, and any encountered issues.

Provide Support and Training to Pilot Users: Offer comprehensive support and training sessions to the pilot users to ensure they understand how to use the DevX Wallet effectively and can provide informed feedback.

Analyze Feedback and Prioritize Feature Enhancements and Bug Fixes: Review and analyze the collected feedback to identify common issues and areas for improvement. Prioritize these findings to guide the next phase of development, focusing on feature enhancements and critical bug fixes.
title: Pilot Phase and User Feedback Collection

description:
Complete the structuring and documentation for the tokenization.


All documentation is drafted explicitly with Cardano as the intended underlying blockchain. These documents remain fully compliant with German and EU law and are reusable as regulatory templates for future Cardano-based RWA projects.


A. Factsheet electronic security — Redacted factsheet compliant with the German Securities Trading Act (WpHG §§ 63-64) and BaFin guidelines on financial advertising, covering:

   a. Authorization and Registration: Securities Register § 16 eWpG, Custody and Registration Approval.

   b. Asset Definition: type of asset, underlying asset characteristics, valuation methodology, token representation, custody and storage, asset segregation, regulatory status, liquidity and redemption conditions.

   c. Security Design: token type and issuing blockchain (Cardano), rights attached to tokens, issuance and redemption process, transferability and trading, smart contract terms, governance and control mechanisms, investor protection measures (AML/KYC), data storage and reporting, eWpG and BaFin compliance including cybersecurity, token supply and allocation, auditing and transparency.

   d. Investor Information (WpHG Compliance): mandatory disclosures per WpHG, product information and risk disclosures per §§ 31 and 31a WpHG.

   e. Legal and Regulatory Compliance: jurisdiction and governing law, AML/KYC procedures per GwG, prospectus exemption information per Prospectus Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, reporting and disclosure obligations.

   f. Investor Rights and Protections: creditor protections per eWpG limited recourse rules, risk disclosures (market, operational, regulatory, issuer-specific), liquidity and exit options.

   g. Technical and Operational Security: Cardano blockchain specifications, scalability, § 25a KWG cybersecurity measures, data backup, integrity, and disaster recovery.

   h. Distribution and Offering: target investor profile, selling restrictions, distribution period and offering terms.

   i. Reporting and Regulatory Oversight: reporting to BaFin and Deutsche Bundesbank including audits, BaFin oversight of issuance and distribution.

   j. Clarity and Transparency: all essential information presented clearly for retail investors per § 31 WpHG.


B. Offering Document via Securities Information Sheet (WIB) — Redacted WIB based on the prospectus exemption under WpPG / Article 3(2) Prospectus Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 (issuance volume not exceeding EUR 8 million over 12 months), prepared per §§ 13–17 VermAnlG, maximum 3 pages, factual and free of marketing language, covering:

   a. Title and Purpose.

   b. Scope and prospectus exemption.

   c. Product Description.

   d. Investment Objectives and Strategies.

   e. Issuer Information.

   f. Target Market.

   g. Risk Information.

   h. Return Potential and Loss Risks.

   i. Key Terms and Conditions.

   j. Costs and Fees.

   k. Taxation.

   l. Conflicts of Interest.

   m. Regulatory Information.

   n. Contact Information.


C. Key Information Document (PRIIPs KID) — Redacted KID mandated by PRIIPs Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 / Article 5, provided to retail investors before investment, in a clear, standardized, and comparable format, covering:

   a. Title and Purpose.

   b. Product Overview (product name, manufacturer, ISIN, contact information).

   c. Objectives and Target Investor.

   d. Risk and Reward Profile (standardized risk indicator).

   e. Performance Scenarios (favorable, moderate, unfavorable).

   f. Costs (entry, ongoing, exit costs with examples).

   g. Recommended Holding Period and Early Exit.

   i. How to Complain.

   j. Other Relevant Information.


Clarification on Redacted form


Publishing the documents in a redacted form means that certain sensitive, proprietary, or confidential information has been removed or obscured. Redactions may include:


1. Personal and Contact Information: Any specific names, direct contact details, or addresses unnecessary for general understanding.

2. Confidential Financial Data: Details about pricing, proprietary valuation methodologies, or specific financial figures.

3. Proprietary Techniques and IP: Any proprietary tokenization processes, unique blockchain structures, or specific smart contract terms.

4. Regulatory Details Beyond Compliance Requirements: Extensive internal compliance notes or detailed legal strategies not required for public understanding.

acceptance_criteria:
Requirements must clearly and completely encompass the full range of the user experience, with examples of key workflows from beginning to end across at least 3 use cases.

Key workflows include:

  1. Vault formation: Vaults are user-configurable smart contracts ("SC") that allow users to send on-chain assets (NFTs, FTs) to the SC, to be locked until certain criteria are met, or until the transaction is cancelled. Users who establish the Vault SCs are the "Admin" users of each vault.
  2. Fractionalization: The process by which 3rd party users will send ADA to the SC and receive newly minted fractional tokens ("FTs") in exchange for the ADA, based on the settings and criteria established by the Admin.
  3. Governance: The process by which FT holders can exhibit ownership functions impacting the assets held in the SCs.

The requirements should outline these key workflows with user stories covering the following: (1) One NFT Asset Fractionalization, (2) Multiple NFT Asset Fractionalization, (3) Basket of Fungible Native Token Assets Fractionalization.

description:
The goals of this milestone include:

  • Atlas to have it's own coin selection algorithm, as:
  • Current algorithm is out-sourced from cardano-wallet repository, available here. We aim to implement a custom variant which would give us greater flexibility and better serve our use-case.
  • Own coin selection algorithm also helps us reduce build dependencies, as we would not require dependency upon `cardano-wallet`'s sub-libraries. Less dependency bloat would enable us to more promptly support version updates to GHC (flagship Haskell compiler).
  • Current coin selection algorithm is tied deeply with transaction fee estimate cycle, we aim to improve on that so we can reduce from current logarithmic fee estimate iterations to something more constant.
  • UTxO caching to better manage back-to-back transactions. This is relevant if transactions are submitted quickly in succession.
  • Improved transaction chaining and parallel transaction building abstractions.
  • Improvements to data providers supported by Atlas.
  • Improvements to Atlas test framework. Currently Atlas supports two frameworks, a private testnet connected to locally ran node and a simulated mock testnet via clb. We would like to provide interoperability where one can write test in a unified language and configure different backend test framework to execute it under.
title: Improvements spanning Coin Selection, dependencies bloat, test framework, etc.

description:
The goals of this milestone are:

  • To make Atlas compile with GHC version 9.10.1 or later.
  • It's worth noting that currently, Atlas compiles with GHC version 9.6.5, which lacks some of the features added by GHC 9.10.1 in relevance to JavaScript and WebAssembly backends as a GHC compilation target.
  • Exploration and utilisation of Atlas on client side in browsers.
  • Currently if one is to make use of Atlas, it is not possible to run it entirely on client side in web browsers but rather one would need to make an API endpoint available from the server backend which the browser client can then call. This is one important difference with off-chain transaction building tools that target JavaScript. GHC 9.10.1 provides useful compilation targets such as WASM & JS with JS FFI interoperability. We aim to make use of these targets and FFI compatibilities to enable Atlas to run entirely on client side.
title: Support of the latest GHC version (9.10.1 or later) and browser client-side support

• Region, Asset and Custody selection must be determined as viable and preferable relative to the alternatives. The selection process should take the form of discussion and documented analysis. The analysis will be performed by senior Genius Yield staff in conjunction with RWA industry specialists. The full set of considered options and the selected outcomes should be documented with justifications. Included in the document should be stated the criteria by which the selection was established. The initial asset and regional selection criteria should be guided by the path of least regulational and financial resistance towards the goal of a functional RWA issuance and exchange platform which can be further expanded upon over time.


  • The term `region` in this documentation refers to the possible financial regulatory authorities by jurisdiction as subscribed to by nation states and nation state unions. Please see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_financial_regulatory_authorities_by_jurisdiction


  • The legal agreement Jurisdictional compliance will be determined by the requirements set forth by the selected region / nation state or nation state union and their associated regulatory bodies. It is difficult to be more specific at the time of writing on which regions will be selected during the milestone. There is a high likelihood that we will start with the region of Luxembourg to develop the legal framework requirements as initial research and consultation has indicated that it is a preferable Jurisdiction for RWA issuance and exchange regulation. The long term aim of the project is to support many regions and Jurisdictions, however regional support is predicated on the benefits the regional support represents. Over time we aim to expand our jurisdictional coverage and grow the application and organisation as we discover the regulatory landscape.


  • In order to investigate possible unknowns, legal and RWA industry experts will be provided with documentation and be invited to comment where possible to resolve known unknowns. In addition they will be invited to comment on any topics which they believe we have omitted due to being unknown by the authors (unknown unknowns). The documentation which will be provided to said experts consists of:
  • The selected asset type(s) and region(s).
  • A set of cases which are known unknowns and relating questions.
  • A high level description of the technical solution we have in mind for RWA as it relates to the block chain.


  • The documentation or data required to determine ownership should determine ownership clearly and to the extent required by the agreement to meet the objective of transferring ownership rights.


  • Legal agreement(s) must be developed in conjunction with legal experts and verified as legally sound and binding.


  • The legal framework will be established through whichever means are the most appropriate as determined by the most relevant parties to consult. Consultation will take the form of paid and volunteered collaboration with partners and relevant parties in the ecosystem. As communication is likely to cross borders, consultation will take the form of online meetings, emails, and collaborative documentation tools like: Google docs, confluence ect. However we cannot at this stage be more specific about the exact instruments as the third parties likely poses their own preferences and perhaps more appropriate tooling and as such we will not be overly prescriptive.


  • This milestone will follow the following roadmap:
  1. Research and Initial Selection
  2. Regulatory and Legal Analysis
  3. Technical solution regulatory alignment analysis
  4. Data and Documentation Requirements
  5. Legal Agreement Drafting

Attempting to support all regions and assets would not be viable. In order to build a functional RWA platform on which to expand we must endeavour to find the path of least regulatory and financial resistance.


2) Sub-output: In conjunction with legal experts investigate and identify current unknowns and constraints relating to digitization of selected asset(s) ownership in the selected region(s). Eg: Uncontrolled RWA ownership transfer (inheritance, repossession, seizure, ownership dispute resolution). The due diligence relating to asset ownership tokenization unknowns could have implications on the smart contract token controls and actions as well as influence the legal agreement. More cannot be said at this stage as unknowns are by definition unknown and the effect of said unknowns are difficult to predict.


3) Sub-output: In conjunction with legal and selected asset type experts identify the data or documentation required to determine ownership of said asset and which will be referenced in the legal agreement.

description:
The objective of this milestone is to isolate the designs and requirements of a stand alone on-boarding application in the form of documentation and then to develop said on-boarding application. The aim of the on-boarding application is to:

Elicit all the required data from a prospective asset owner that wishes to tokenize their real world asset. Once the owner entity data is collected, KYC must be performed to ensure that the entity meets the requirements of the legal agreement. The application should not allow rejected KYC entities to continue the process. If refused a refusal message should be displayed.

Once KYC is passed the entity will be allowed to enter data required to identify or verify an ownership claim. This information will then be used to verify the entities claim to the asset using the process researched and developed in milestone 2. If refused a refusal message should be displayed.

Once the asset ownership claim is verified the tokenization minting details should be elicited from the user. This includes but is not limited to the number of tokens to be minted. The token mint options must align with the constraints set forth in the legal agreement.

Finally to proceed the owner entity will have to agree to and submit the legal agreement.

Only once the entire on-boarding process described in this milestone is completed and a reviewer has assessed all required data would RWA minting be performed.


1) Sub-output: Create documentation describing the full on-boarding process, including:

  • Figma UI designs for the full process
  • Asset owner entity data requirements
  • KYC service data requirements
  • Asset owner KYC gate keeping requirements
  • Asset data requirements
  • Asset gate keeping requirements
  • Token minting data requirements
  • Legal agreement data requirements


2) Main-output: Develop an onboarding web application (UI/UX) to perform the follow in sequence:

  1. Elicit owner entity data via digital forms
  2. Perform KYC on owner entity utilising third party KYC services
  3. Gate keep asset owners via KYC results that do not meet contractual requirements
  4. Elicit asset data via digital forms
  5. Verify asset ownership via process developed in Milestone 2)
  6. Gate keep assets that do not meet contractual requirements
  7. Elicit intended tokenization data via digital forms.
  8. Complete legal agreement developed in Milestone 1) to transfer ownership.


3) Main-output: Develop an admin page which allows reviewers to authenticate to gain access. The admin application should list RWA applicants and the extent to which they have met the on-boarding process, exposing the relevant applicant data. Authorised reviewers should be able through the application to confirm that the applicant has meet the data requirements to move forward in the application process. The approved status should be communicated to the applicant via the on-boarding application UI.


4) Sub-output: Deploy the on-boarding web application to a private testing environment. The application deployed to the test environment must operate in a test mode such that testing the application does not result in testers being bound to legal agreements or having to actually verify ownership of personal assets.
title: Digital onboarding Pipeline Application

acceptance_criteria:
The acceptance criteria of the on-chain technical implementation is difficult if not impossible to fully specify at this stage as consultation is milestone 1 will determine the regulatory details which will govern exactly how the on chain RWA assets are required to be constrained. For that reason the acceptance criteria defined here must be at a relatively high level as it is not yet possible to be more specific on many of the yet to be determined implementation details.

1. Minting RWA Assets

  • The service must support creating transactions that mint new RWA tokens.
  • The service must provide a mechanism to link RWA tokens to their underlying real-world assets through verifiable metadata.

2. Burning RWA Assets

  • The service must support creating transactions that burn RWA tokens.
  • The service must ensure that burning transactions remove the tokens from circulation accurately and update the ledger accordingly.

3. Transferring RWA Assets

  • The service must support creating transactions to transfer RWA tokens between addresses.
  • The service must validate that the sender has sufficient balance of the specific RWA tokens before creating the transaction.
  • The service must ensure that transfers comply with ownership and transferability rules specified by the associated securities regulatory body.

4. Regulatory Compliance

  • The service must provide functionality to include regulatory compliance data in the transaction metadata.

5. The RWA on-chain documentation must describe exhaustively all state transitions, required data and meta data requirements.
description:
The objective of this milestone is to develop all block chain domain technologies relating to the RWA assets to be issued. This includes all smart contract development and transaction building systems for all aspects of the RWA life cycle, however at the time of writing the details RWA life cycle are not fully understood and will be dependent on the outcome discoveries of the regulatory investigation which take part in milestone 1.

What is known is we require mechanisms to perform the following in a regulatory compliant manner:

  • The ability to mint onchain assets which will represent the RWA assets ownership rights.
  • The ability to transfer said assets.
  • The ability to burn said assets.
  • What is unknown at this stage is:
  • Whether RSA tokens will be represented as native cardano assets.
  • How token transfer will be controlled.
  • Whether native tokens will be permitted into a users wallet.
  • How RWA asset transactions will be controlled.
  • Under what conditions will RWA asset be permitted to be burnt.

Ideally we will make use of Cardano native tokens and constrain the tokens such that they can only be transferred if approval is granted by a licensed securities exchange authority, however this technical direction must be validated with legal and securities experts to confirm viability as part of the expert consultation to take place in milestone 1. If not sufficient we will have to develop a more conventional approach to meet the requirements of the on-chain RWA life cycle, which do not necessarily limit RWA transfers between wallets. More cannot be determined at the time of writing.

To note the transaction building development will leverage the existing GY transaction building services, which comprise of a dedicated internal REST API server for said purposes.

1) Sub output: Develop documentation which described the full state machine life cycle for on chain RWA assets.

2) Main output:

  • Develop on-chain RWA mint contract functionality.
  • Develop on-chain RWA burn contract functionality (The mint and burn contract could be the same contract).
  • Develop on-chain RWA token transfer contract functionality.

4) Main output:

  • Develop RWA token transfer approval mechanism (optional requirement).

5) Main output:

  • Develop RWA mint transaction building systems.
  • Develop RWA burn transaction building systems.
  • Develop RWA transfer transaction building systems.
title: RWA token issuance, restrictions and transfer

acceptance_criteria:

  • RWA swap technical spec should address all significant technical unknowns, which must be determined before development starts.

KYC Data Requirements:

  • Clear specifications of the data required from the user to perform KYC, including personal information and documentation requirements.
  • KYC Process:
  • Detailed steps outlining the entire KYC process from data collection to verification and approval.

Trader KYC Integration Partner:

  • Identification and description of the integration with the chosen KYC partner, including API endpoints and data flow.
  • Trader KYC Gatekeeping Requirements:
  • Criteria and mechanisms to ensure that only KYC-verified users can perform swaps or claim income.

Initial Whitelisted Native Assets:

  • A comprehensive list of initial native assets allowed for exchange, including necessary details about each asset.

2) Application:

  • Authentication/KYC Page:
  • Must allow users to complete the KYC process if not already done.
  • Users should receive clear feedback on the status of their KYC process (e.g., pending, approved, or rejected).
  • KYC verification should be integrated and functional with the specified KYC partner.

RWA Swap Page:

  • Must display a list of RWA assets owned by the authenticated user.
  • Must show a history of RWA transactions specific to the user.
  • Users must be able to create limit orders to buy/sell RWA assets, with orders restricted to whitelisted assets.
  • Ensure users without successful KYC verification are prevented from creating limit orders.
  • Must include a functional order book representation of limit orders.
  • Should feature a dynamic and interactive candle price chart for RWA assets.

- RWA Claim Page:

  • Must display accumulated income available for claim, categorized by RWA asset.
  • Should show a history of income claims, also categorized by RWA asset.
  • Ensure users without successful KYC verification are prevented from claiming RWA income.

3) Final Closeout:

  • The report is made publicly available via a link to report documentation.
  • The video is made publicly available via a link to online video content.
description:
The objective of this milestone is to deliver as an output a public facing web application (UI/UX). The application application should facilitate three main pages and objectives: KYC / authentication, RWA swaps, and RWA income claims.

In this milestone we will modify and reuse as a blue print existing genius yield swap and reward systems where possible to facilitate trading of RWA tokens and revenue distribution. The RWA swap application will make use of existing genius yield decentralised finance platforms and reward mechanisms but will be developed in a standalone manner to isolate the application and avoid a monolithic architecture, isolating shared dependencies where necessary.

Users will be required to perform KYC and only be permitted to perform swap transactions or RWA income claims if the KYC requirements determined in milestone 1 are met.

1) Sub-output: Create application documentation describing:

  • Figma UI designs for the layout / navbar / wallet connection components
  • Figma UI designs for the KYC / authentication page
  • Figma UI designs for the RWA swap page
  • Figma UI designs for the RWA income claim page
  • Minimal feature requirements
  • Minimal technical specification
  • Communication protocol type (REST API, GraphQL, RPC, ect) between client and server
  • Communication protocol data fetch schema definitions
  • Trader KYC data requirements
  • Trader KYC process
  • Trader KYC integration partner
  • Trader KYC gatekeeping requirements
  • Describe initial whitelisted native assets which can be exchanged for RWA assets

2) Main-output: Create application featuring:

  • Authentication / KYC page
  • Component which allows users to perform KYC process if it has not been performed
  • A RWA swap page
  • Component to list RWA assets owned by authenticated user
  • Component to list historic RWA transactions by authenticated user
  • Component to create limit order to buy or sell RWA asset in exchange for other whitelisted native assets
  • Gatekeep limit order creation if user has not successfully met KYC requirements
  • Component to display a representation of the orderbook of RWA limit orders
  • Component to display a candle price chart
  • A RWA claim page
  • Component to list accumulated income that can be Claimed grouped by RWA asset
  • Component to list historic income claims grouped by RWA asset
  • Gatekeep RWA claims if user has not successfully met KYC requirements

3) Final close-out:

  • Report
  • Video
title: RWA Swap Application

acceptance_criteria:
Hydra research and risk assessment will provide indication of any potential limitation of Hydra from both functional and non-functional perspectives. The purpose of the system is to sustain a significant number of users, hence having understanding of number of users / merchants we can sustain using one hydra head is key in modelling any scaling solutions. Other questions to be answered: limits for adding utxos to heads and how to most efficiently query information from the Hydra head.

The accounting system design and architecture document will describe key architectural viewpoints, technologies and frameworks to be used, as well as how the books and records system will be orchestrated in the hydra head via individual utxos. Funds management including funds release to layer 1 from the head details will also be detailed as part of the document. Another aspect to be tackled will be how to decentralise the funds custody.

The wireframes will undergo a number of ideation iterations in true agile fashion with clients and wineries. To validate the quality, we shall conduct a user validation testing round with several non-involved initially wineries and users to capture additional feedback on usability. The design for the app will include wireframes for each page including navigation flows between respective pages.

*This reflects the transition from the originally described pull-request–based onboarding mechanism to a self-serve cryptographic registration flow, as approved in the Change Request. The measurable objective remains dynamic project onboarding via SDK-supported mechanisms.

Traceability note (Change Request alignment):

*The original proposal referenced a pull-request–based onboarding mechanism coordinated through repository governance. Following the approved Change Request, onboarding is implemented through a self-serve cryptographic registration flow, enabling projects to authenticate and register directly via signed transactions or cryptographic verification.

**In the initial proposal, reputation logic was described in a more centrally defined structure. The updated architecture allows participating projects to define and configure their own reputation metrics within the Statur framework, while preserving verifiability and transparency of score calculation.

***The original description implied reputation updates tied to fixed epoch or month-based cycles. The updated implementation introduces configurable preset update intervals defined at the project level, maintaining predictable update behavior while increasing architectural flexibility.

description:
In Japan, legal revisions have been made to allow for the establishment of DAOs and the operation of businesses by utilizing an LLC. However, the establishment of a DAO involves issues related to Japan's Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and Companies Act. Additionally, if tokens are to be issued, the Payment Services Act will also be a concern. Violations can result in severe penalties. Furthermore, when operating a DAO, if the appropriate articles of incorporation and regulations are not created, it could be legally invalid.

Therefore, it is essential to have a lawyer scrutinize the legal compliance based on the purpose of the DAO, the content of the tokens to be issued, and the method of organizational management. First, we will determine the purpose of the DAO, the content of the tokens to be issued, and the method of organizational management in consultation with DAO experts. Based on the purpose of the DAO, the content of the tokens to be issued, and the method of organizational management, we will ensure legal compliance, create the necessary articles of incorporation and regulations, and establish an LLC-based DAO (Million Member DAO LLC, "MMD") as a corporation in Japan.

※The name has been changed from FJTW DAO to Million Member DAO (MMD). MMD will be the main DAO.

At the same time, we will have community managers join Discord and grant them community manager NFTs.

Following this, as a kick-off event for MMD, we will hold the following events.

The following event will be held in Kagawa, which is under consideration for becoming a web3 special zone and is the constituency of the first Digital Minister Hirai, head of the Digital Society Promotion Headquarters, and to which the first Digital Minister Hirai has been invited.

acceptance_criteria: The new transaction builder is capable of submitting all the relevant kinds of transactions for Kwarxs to the Cardano testnet (preprod or preview). Specifically, it is capable of performing the two main user actions: minting the NFTs giving rights to receive a share of the shared profits and claiming the portion of rewards to which the NFT holder is entitled.
description:
The current implementation of the code to build transactions has three components: the backend transaction builder, a minting signature bot and the frontend adapter for partial transactions. These components make use of the deprecated library Bot Plutus Interface. The main purpose of this milestone is to simplify the design by unifying the code for building transactions and also moving away from unmaintained libraries. Our first option is to use Atlas, as we believe it will provide the easiest migration path given the state of our current implementation.

As such, the output of Milestone 1 is:

  • Refactored code for building transactions that uses Atlas (or an alternative maintained library) and has a simplified architecture with less components.
title: Refactor the transaction builder to simplify design and move away from unmaintained libraries

acceptance_criteria:
• The new transaction builder is capable of submitting all the relevant kinds of transactions for Kwarxs to the Sancho Network, the testnet supporting Cardano’s Conway era. Specifically, it is capable of performing the two main user actions: minting the NFTs giving rights to receive a share of the shared profits and claiming the portion of rewards to which the NFT holder is entitled.


Note that in the event that Milestone 2 is submitted after the Chang hardfork has taken place, submitting transactions to the preview network will be considered equivalent to submitting them to the Sancho Network.
description:
Following the refactor in Milestone 1, the code will be in a good position to support future versions of Cardano, including the upcoming Conway era. In this milestone, the transaction builder will be adapted to be compatible with the Sancho network, which is the beacon for the Conway era. Once transactions submitted to the Sancho network are accepted, the code will be prepared to run smoothly even post Chang hard-fork.

As such, the output of Milestone 2 is:

  • Transaction builder that supports building transactions compatible with the Conway era.
title: Update the transaction builder to support the Conway era.

acceptance_criteria:
• Transactions interacting with the Kwarxs on-chain scripts via the frontend can be submitted to the Sancho Network using at least 2 different light wallets.
  • A transaction claiming rewards in bulk (i.e. rewards from more than 1 NFT owned by the same address) can be submitted to the Sancho Network.
  • Users that have their wallet connected can see the aggregated amount of claimable rewards by all their Kwarxs NFTs.
  • The Kwarxs website displays information about the solar farms in operation.

Note: In order to kick-start the process, Kwarxs is committing to a power plant operating from day 1 with the following metrics:

  • Total capacity: 74.6 KWp
  • Size: 766 sqm
  • Number of solar modules: 1,036 modules
  • Annual energy production: 78,000 KWh
  • Performance ratio: 87%
  • CO2 reduction per year: 45.5 tons
  • Feed-in tariff: 0.349 cents / kWh
  • Commissioning date: Year 2009
  • Payback period: 9.5 years

The investment for this power plant has been fully paid back and as such it does not represent a liability for Kwarxs NFT holders. Therefore, NFT holders start benefiting from the revenue generated by this power plant from day 1. While metrics for a successful 2024 are similar to the ones listed above, the size of the project will grow as proceeds from NFT sales are used to commission new power plants.
description:
The current implementation of the frontend will be updated to use the new API developed in Milestones 1 and 2, as well as enhanced with new functionality such as support for bulk claiming of rewards and increased display of information related to the user NFTs and Kwarxs operations.

As such, the outputs of Milestone 3 are:

  • Integration of the frontend with the updated library for building transactions.
  • Enhanced functional frontend from where transactions can be submitted using a variety of light wallets.
  • Support for bulk claiming of rewards.
  • Visualisation of claimable rewards by users.
  • Information about Kwarxs operations in real life, which provide the basis for the utility associated with the NFTs. The displayed information will include key operational, environmental and financial metrics of the power plants such as:
  • Total capacity of the plant, showing the system’s power capacity and its ability to generate solar energy.
  • Size of the solar plant, highlighting the physical scale of the project.
  • Number of solar modules, illustrating the extent of the installation and its technology.
  • Annual energy production, demonstrating how much clean energy is generated each year.
  • Performance ratio, reflecting the efficiency of the plant.
  • CO2 reduction per year, highlighting the environmental impact of the project through avoided greenhouse gas emissions.
  • Feed-in tariff, showing the economic viability and financial return from feeding electricity into the grid.
  • Commissioning date, indicating the age of the plant.
  • Payback period, showing the time for recovery of investment costs.
title: Updated and enhanced frontend.

Also, the NFT metadata such as associated images and videos will be pre-processed and hosted in IPFS.

As such, the outputs of Milestone 4 are:

Documentation detailing the incentive program point system including: 

  • how to qualify for rewards
  • what types of actions are required to gain points
  • how we plan to balance the point distribution
  • how much time the incentive program will last
  • how points will be calculated and distributed
  • how much rewards are going to be disbursed during this program
  • how we plan to track and manage bot and excessive activity

Contextual Notes: Apart from the fixes, there are some changes being made with this last submission of SoM. 

Mainly: it is about the removal of certain actions to qualify for points during the incentive program.

The inclusion of such actions such as providing liquidity or bridging would make the program overly complicated for the development side as well as participation. It would also dilute the low rewards to the point it may make participating in the program not even worth it. For the Wanchain part, we plan on still including the incentives from Wanchain, but it will be handled by Wanchain and not part of this program.

We want this program to be an initiative that is replicable and useful in the future, and can be applied to other projects. For the Cardano ecosystem, the number one priority should be increasing on chain volumes, and we want that to be the only focus with this program.

Hence we have made the decision to focus only on trading volume as the measure which will determine points. This is similar to other Trading incentivization programs in the past such as this one from snek: https://www.snek.com/trading-competition

The Incentive Program should focus purely on the Trading volume of users.

The more elements the program has, the more difficult it is to deliver. It also makes it harder from a user experience. 

In addition, considering the economic incentives are relatively low, the more actions we include in the program, the less it makes sense for users to participate, as it increases their cost which might even be higher than their rewards. 

We are in close relationship with Wanchain, who are still happy to proceed with this program and bring their own incentives (please confirm with them directly if you would like).

However, it doesn't make sense to include bridging as one of the actions in the points system, for the reasons mentioned above (higher cost, longer delivery, complexity for users, diversification of incentives making them less effective, etc.)

Hence, this update to SoM removes any mentions of adding and removing liquidity, as well as bridging it from other ecosystems.

The work will be conducted mostly manually, accompanied with tailored analysis tools.
title: Edge Case Identification

acceptance_criteria:

  • Quantitative Breakdown of Vulnerabilities: All vulnerabilities identified, with each categorized by severity.
  • Detailed Recommendations: A specific fix or mitigation strategy provided for each identified vulnerability.
  • Incorporation of Best Practices: Best practice recommendations relevant to OpShin development.

OpShin Team Feedback and Integration:

  • Feedback Collection: Written feedback from the OpShin team is collected and added to the report.
  • Codebase Integration: Evidence that the OpShin team has addressed all critical and high-severity issues in the codebase, demonstrated by commits, pull requests, or updated documentation.
description:
The audit team compiles a comprehensive audit report detailing identified vulnerabilities, recommended fixes, and best practices for OpShin development.

These educational resources will cater to non-technical users as the main source of information for not only learning how to utilize the ODAO toolkit but to understand the system design decisions that sets it apart from existing alternatives and how novel features being introduced will be used to propel the quality and impact of DAO governance on Cardano. description:
The technical specification from the first milestone will be implemented using Aiken and/or PlutusV3, the leading Cardano smart contract programming languages in the ecosystem, to develop the core sets of smart contracts for the OToken Framework. The number of smart contracts will be determined by the scope of the system as it is implemented, and it’s based on the developers preferred method of organizing their codebase. The entire logic of the system could be implemented into just one smart contract, but it could also be better organized by splitting into smaller components. Our developers will use leading software engineering best practices when deciding the optimal number of smart contracts to best encapsulate the entirety of the system.

This open sourced codebase will be deployed on a private testnet or on a the mainnet with limited assets for internal verification and thorough testing of system logic, core  mechanisms and key components. A video walkthrough describing the general functionalities of these smart contracts will be presented where the lead developer will explain a high level overview of the OToken system for Catalyst reviewers and other non-technical audiences to familiarize themselves with the codebase.

Additionally, the value of the partnership and collaboration is clear through: DigiFarm would produce the data-set based on remote sensing SatEO (Sentinel-2 at 1m resolution), field boundaries and seeded acres along with vegetation/production (yield data on a field by field basis) in a database, which would then be used for NMKR to fetch the data through (a) developing the API response (b) mint the non-fungible tokens (NFTs) for each individual field boundary which will be enriched with the meta-data specified © connecting with other data sources. The acceptance criteria can be documented as the the additional value of bringing the data-set onto the blockchain/NFTs and the transaction volume or additional value to the agricultural value-chain and ecosystem (i.e. reduction of cost in manual data silos which exists now, lack of transparency, significant presence of errors in data-set in current framework etc.)

Comprehensive Architectural Plan:

  • The architectural plan must:
  • Clearly define the microservices architecture, including service definitions, communication protocols, and data storage solutions.
  • Detail the smart contract architecture, specifying the functions automated by smart contracts, the interaction between smart contracts and backend services, and how logging listener enforces data integrity and compliance.
  • Detail the security framework, including encryption standards, access control mechanisms, and audit trails.
  • Include a scalability analysis that discusses potential bottlenecks and mitigation strategies.
  • Provide a detailed explanation of how the system will ensure data integrity through (Cardano) blockchain anchoring, with clear steps and technical specifications.
  • The plan should be reviewed and validated by at least two independent technical experts from the cardano community, with documented feedback and responses.

Detailed System Process and Interaction Diagrams:

  • Diagrams must:
  • Accurately reflect the system’s architecture and provide a clear visual representation of data flows, service interactions, and user interactions.
