description:
Comprehensive Architectural Plan for Backend Integration:

  • Develop a detailed architectural blueprint that integrates backend systems with the Cardano blockchain. This blueprint will focus on achieving high scalability, security, and data integrity specifically tailored for the Forensic Management System.

Key Components:

Diagrams illustrating below:

  • Microservices Architecture:
  • Define a microservices-based approach where each service within the Forensic Management System is modular, independently deployable, and scalable.
  • Service discovery and load balancing methods to manage traffic across microservices.


  • Database and Storage Solutions:
  • Implementation of a scalable and distributed database solution, such as PostgreSQL or a NoSQL database like supabase, to handle large volumes of forensic data.
  • Design of data partitioning strategies for efficient querying and retrieval, ensuring data locality and minimizing latency.


  • Security and Compliance Framework:
  • Incorporate end-to-end encryption for data at rest and in transit. This will include implementing encryption algorithms that comply with industry standards such as AES-256 for data storage.
  • Design an access control layer using RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) that integrates with existing identity providers to manage user permissions effectively.
  • Implement logging (audit trails) for all user actions and system processes, ensuring that all interactions with forensic evidence are logged, immutable, and traceable for compliance purposes.


  • Smart Contract Architecture:
  • Design and implement smart contracts that interact with critical functions within the Forensic Management System, such as evidence submission, validation, and access control.
  • A logging listener will record all the logs for transactions happening to the smart contract for compliance puposes.
  • Integration of these smart contracts with the backend system, ensuring seamless communication and data exchange between the contracts and the microservices.
title: System Architecture Design

acceptance_criteria:
• Functional Prototype with Blockchain Integration:
  • The prototype must include a fully functioning evidence registration system that generates SHA-256 hashes. These hashes represents the relationship between the case number, aliases, and subaliases.
  • The system must store these hashes on the Cardano blockchain, creating a verifiable and immutable audit trail.
  • The prototype should demonstrate the automated triggering of smart contracts for evidence status updates, with clear, verifiable blockchain transactions for each action. The smart contracts should specifically handle conditions such as evidence submission, validation, and retrieval.
  • The system should provide a user interface that allows interaction with the evidence management process, showing the end-to-end workflow from evidence registration to blockchain stamping.
  • Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) Implementation:
  • The ZKP feature must be fully implemented within the prototype, allowing for the verification of the relationship between the case number, aliases, and subaliases without revealing the actual content of the evidence.
  • The ZKP implementation should be demonstrated in a specific scenario where the authenticity and integrity of confidential information are verified while keeping the actual data private.
  • The prototype must generate detailed logs and records showing how ZKP is applied, with blockchain transactions that ensure only verified information is stamped onto the blockchain without exposing any private data.
description:
• Functional Prototype Development:
  • Develop a functional prototype that demonstrates the integration of the forensic management system with the Cardano blockchain. This prototype will include key features that ensure data integrity, immutability, and confidentiality using advanced cryptographic techniques.
  • Features Included in the Prototype:
  • Evidence Registration with Hash Generation (SHA-256):
  • Implement a feature that automatically generates a SHA-256 hash showcasing the relationship between Case number, aliases and subaliases.
  • The system will store the hash on the Cardano blockchain, creating a verifiable audit trail for each piece of evidence.
  • Automated Smart Contract Triggers for Evidence Status Updates:
  • Develop and deploy smart contracts that automatically trigger status updates based on specific conditions (e.g., evidence submission, validation, or retrieval).
  • These smart contracts will interact with the backend system to enforce the integrity and transparency of the evidence management process.
  • Blockchain Transactions for Evidence Log Entries:
  • Record every evidence log entry as a transaction on the Cardano blockchain, ensuring that each action is traceable and cannot be altered retroactively.
  • This will involve developing a mechanism that links each transaction with the corresponding evidence entry and its hash.
  • Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) for Confidential Evidence Verification:
  • Implement a ZKP feature that allows for the verification of relationship between Case number, aliases and subaliases without revealing the actual content of the evidence. This will ensure that sensitive information remains confidential while still providing proof of integrity and authenticity.
  • The ZKP mechanism will be integrated with the blockchain stamping process, ensuring that only verified information is stamped onto the blockchain without exposing any private data.
title: Prototype Development

acceptance_criteria:
1. Criteria. The study shall address:
  2. How to maintain a unique identifiable contract state from one eUTXO to the next such that other contracts can read that state. This service may or may not already be provided by some Cardano contract languages, and may or may not be easy to provide on top of those languages. Presumably, underneath it all, an NFT identifies its holder as having “the” state for the bridge contract, and all lock scripts involved track which eUTXO possesses the NFT and what data is associated with it.
  3. How best to verify multisigs from DA committees. Some elaborate multisig algorithms yield cheaper proofs than others, and may be preferred; yet a simpler though more expensive alternative signature algorithm may be provided as a fallback in case some DA committee members become uncooperative. The report must show how at least one suitable algorithm is supported, and discuss the alternatives.
  4. How to verify in some smart contract language a “merkle proof” that data was present in a merkle tree the root of which was signed, especially 
  5. in connection with using the data as public keys and/or 
  6. as signatures in conjunction with verification (something not directly possible with e.g. BitcoinScript).
  7. Non-Criteria:


  1. The feasibility study should be written at a level that a “person having ordinary skill in the art” of implementing cryptographic protocols should be able to implement an actual prototype:
  2. The specification is informal. It may involve more formal parts, but is not obliged to do so at this feasibility stage:
  3. Parts of the specification, or illustrations thereof may be provided as actual code, be it in Plutus, Plutarch, Aiken, or any smart contract language that supports Cardano.
  4. Parts of the specification can be written in a language that does not support Cardano or is not meant for smart contracts.
  5. Parts of the specification may even be pseudo code that is not in any actual language.
  6. Parts of the specification can remain entirely in English.
  7. Parts of the specification can use code or pseudo-code as illustration only rather than specification.
  8. The specification, whether code, pseudo-code or English description may elide some corner cases, or some checks necessary for robustness.
  9. The specification can entirely ignore some features of the Data Availability network such as verifying that a ledger properly maintains the accounting of stakes and fees. Such features can presumably be implemented in a straightforward way using arithmetic operators and basic data structures provided by the programming language.
  10. ﻿﻿The specification from this feasibility study is not meant as an exact blueprint for the future system that will bind its developers. After implementing, testing and debugging the system, in subsequent milestones and beyond, the result may differ considerably from this specification along many dimensions, including a different choice of cryptographic algorithms or merkleized data structures, bug fixes, improvements to performance, robustness, security or maintainability, etc. Still, best effort will be made to ensure that the choice of algorithms made in this initial specification should hopefully remain relevant in the actual implementation.

Criteria:

  1. The deliverable is to demonstrate the basic infrastructure for stateful interaction with and between two smart contracts, one for the DA bridge, one for a DA client—roughly corresponding to section 1)a) of the specification from Milestone 1, "How to maintain a unique identifiable contract state from one eUTXO to the next such that other contracts can read that state." All other details are subordinate to the implementation and validation of this infrastructure.
  2. The smart contracts should build, and the tests shall pass—at the specified commit.
  3. The tests shall actually have a private Cardano network execute the on-chain smart contract flows of a Data Availability interaction, including:
  4. The bridge updating the DA merkle root, checking DA committee signatures.
  5. The client validating attestations that some data was published on the DA, using a merkle proof from the DA merkle root stored by the bridge.
  6. Since they must actually run on-chain, the smart contracts must be written in a language that supports Cardano, whichever language we may choose.

Non-criteria:

  1. This deliverable is to demonstrate the basic infrastructure for the Data Availability Network. The signature support and data structure validation can be minimal, maybe even caricaturably underpowered, because they are beside the point of this deliverable.
  2. This deliverable may assume a centralized DA and use oversimplifications for sections 1)b) and 1)c) of the specification("How best to verify multisigs from DA committees," and "How to verify in some smart contract language a 'merkle proof' that data was present in a merkle tree the root of which was signed," respectively): a simple fixed signature may replace a variable multisig, and the merkle proof may assume simplified data structures.
  3. This deliverable as well as all subsequent deliverables may also wholly elide accounting as per Milestone 1 Acceptance Criteria 2)c).
  4. The choice of language in this deliverable shall not be considered either positively or negatively in judging the deliverable, except inasmuch as the language must actually compile down to code executable on Cardano. Our developers will pick which specific language happens to be easiest for them at the time. This choice does not bind us at all to keep using the same language in the future. The future production version of the system may use a different language; it may be written and available in multiple languages that may or may not include the one used in this deliverable. We definitely plan to have at least interfaces if not implementations available in every language that users care about, which may or may not include the language used in this prototype.
  5. No off-chain interaction needs to be implemented for this deliverable, because only the smart contract is being implemented and tested as part of this deliverable, not any actual DA network. The tests can simulate the on-chain component of a Data Availability interaction without any actual data being published on any actual server, without any server being implemented at all. 
  6. The on-chain smart contract parameters used during the test can be precomputed rather than being dynamically computed from an actual DA interaction.

description:
We will produce smart contracts that support a basic Decentralized rather than Centralized Data Availability (“DA”) network, by elaborating on the multisig and merkleized data structure of the DA.


The outputs will consist of an updated github repository at a given commit, containing:

  1. An elaborated Cardano contract for a bridge from a decentralized DA, that accepts updates to the state of the DA.
  2. An accompanying elaborated Cardano contract for a client to this bridge, that verifies the presence of some data in the DA.
  3. Some automated tests that exercise the above contracts.
  4. Instructions on how to build and test the smart contracts.


The purpose of this deliverable is to elaborate on the previous one, so that the bridge may work with a DA network closer to the one that will be used in production. The deliverable may not be “feature complete” with respect to all we may want in production, but it will crucially support decentralization in the DA committees. The deliverable from Milestone 3 will differ from Milestone 2 in the following ways:

Signatures

Milestone 2: Simple signature.

Milestone 3: The DA committee will use a disjunction of multisigs—such that if everything goes right the most efficient one is used, but a less efficient one can be used as a fallback in case some committee members stop cooperating.

Public Keys

Milestone 2: Fixed Set of Public Keys.

Milestone 3: The public keys for the multisig will evolve with time, and the bridge may follow a chain of committees from one to the next, starting from the latest known one.

Data Attestation

Milestone 2: DA committee directly attests a tree of data accepted and republished by the network.

Milestone 3: The DA Committee may attest to a tree of topic committees, with the data in each topic being then attested by its committees, in an indirection. (In the future, there might conceivably be several layers of indirection.)


Once again, running the tests will only involve the on-chain smart contracts, NOT any off-chain service.
title: Demonstration of a Cardano Contract that interacts with a Decentralized Data Availability Committee

acceptance_criteria:
Criteria:

  1. The deliverable is to demonstrate use of the previous smart contracts as part of an ensemble involving an off-chain service and its clients as well as the on-chain smart contracts. All other details are subordinate to the implementation and validation of this ensemble.
  2. In addition to the smart contracts and their on-chain execution, the test cases will include a DA service, a separate data publishing client, and a separate data watching client.
  3. For the purpose of this deliverable, it is enough if the service has a single node only. However, even with a single node, it will still use the DA data structures of a Decentralized network as used by the smart contracts from Milestone 3, including varying committees and multiple topics. While it would be better if the DA service were implemented in a decentralized way with multiple nodes (our eventual goal), that is not in the required scope for this deliverable.
  4. The tests will include end-to-end testing of the DA service, albeit simplified and centralized if need be, with the smart contracts being invoked at appropriate moments.
  5. As contrasted with Milestones 2 and 3, it is essential for Milestone 4 that the on-chain smart contract parameters used during tests be dynamically computed from the interactions, rather than statically precomputed.

Non-criteria:

  1. This deliverable is about testing the previous smart contracts in the dynamic context of a DApp with off-chain as well as on-chain components, where computations are not all precomputed. It is absolutely not about having a feature-complete DA network.
  2. In particular, this deliverable need not improve on the smart contracts from Milestone 3.
  3. Neither the languages used for the off-chain components nor those used for the on-chain smart contracts should be counted either negatively or positively. On-chain and off-chain components alike will be subject to reimplementation as needed before the code hits production.
  4. This milestone is focused on testing the integration of the smart contract with off-chain components, and not the completion of the off-chain components themselves. It does require off-chain interaction, but the off-chain interaction does not need to be decentralized.
description:
We will integrate our smart contract with an early prototype of our DA network to demonstrate an end-to-end test of the contract as part of some interaction involving both on-chain and off-chain components.  The outputs will consist of an updated github repository at a given commit, containing:

  1. A close review, and improvement if necessary (modified or unmodified), for the Cardano contract for a bridge from a decentralized DA that accepts updates to the state of the DA.
  2. An accompanying elaborated Cardano contract for a client to this bridge, whether modified or unmodified, that verifies the presence of some data in the DA.
  3. Code for some DA server that exercises the bridge contract above to update the on-chain state of the DA. The server can be centralized or decentralized.
  4. Code for some DA client that exercises the client contract above to attest on-chain the publication of data on the DA.
  5. Instructions on how to build and test the smart contracts.


The purpose of this deliverable is to demonstrate integration of the on-chain smart contract with an actual off-chain DA service.  However, the DA network need not be complete: 

  • it may be proof-of-authority rather than proof-of-stake, and have only a handful of nodes rather than hundreds or thousands. 
  • It may not fully implement a ledger with staking, and fail to handle payment for publication of data. 
  • It may not have more than a single “topic” on which to publish data. 

Nevertheless, the signatures and data structures it uses will be compatible with those used by the smart contracts, and it will be possible to complete usage flows wherein someone publishes data off-chain on the DA, the DA state is updated on-chain by the DA nodes, and on-chain clients may verify attestations of data publication.


Tests in this milestone WILL involve an actual off-chain service, though that service need not be feature complete, and need not be actually decentralized yet.

acceptance_criteria:
Successful Pool Creation

  • The feature must allow users to create a token pool on the DEX swiftly and successfully, with at least 95% of pool creation attempts completing without errors.

Functionality and Performance Testing

  • Internal testing must confirm that all functionalities perform correctly in at least 95% of test cases.
  • Each function within the pool creation feature must be tested 10 times, with a success rate of 100% in these trials.
  • Performance metrics should show that the pool creation process takes no longer than 30-60 seconds under normal conditions. (Subject to conditions)

User Experience Validation

  • Gather feedback from at least 10 users who test the pool creation feature. At least 90% of these users should report that the process is intuitive and meets their expectations for ease of use.

System Reliability

  • The system must handle at least 50 concurrent pool creation requests without significant degradation in performance, as measured by response time and system stability.

Integration between SNEKbot and Snekx

  • New pool alerts must be successfully integrated between SNEKbot and Snekx and function correctly in 95% of the test scenarios. These alerts should be sent within 5-60 seconds of a pool creation event.
description:
Establishment of Token Trading Pool

  • Successfully establish token trading pools on Splash, Sundae V3, and Minswap V2, ensuring they are fully operational and integrated with the platform.

Integration of New Pool Alerts

  • Implement and integrate new pool alert functionalities between SNEKbot and Snekx, providing users with real-time notifications about new token pools. (As this feature already exists in the SNEKbot infrastructure)
title: DEX Pool Creation Tool

acceptance_criteria:
Functionality and Performance of LP Token Management

  • The system must enable users to burn or lock their LP tokens with a success rate of 95% or higher, measured through multiple (10+) test cases.
  • Burning or locking LP tokens should complete within 10-60 seconds in 90% of the test cases.

Accuracy and Reliability of LP Burn Alerts

  • LP burn alerts integrated with SNEKbot and Snekx must function correctly in 95% of test scenarios, sending notifications within 5 seconds of the burn event.

Efficiency of Metadata Changes

  • The app must allow users to make metadata changes (ticker, description, token image, etc.) with 95% accuracy, validated through multiple (10+) test cases.
  • Metadata changes should be reflected in the app within 10-60 seconds in 90% of the test cases.

User Feedback and Usability Testing

  • Collect feedback from at least 10 users who test the LP token burning, locking, and metadata management features. At least 90% of these users should report that the processes are intuitive and meet their expectations for ease of use and reliability.

Compliance with Industry Standards

  • Ensure all functionalities comply with industry standards for security and reliability, providing detailed documentation and test reports that validate compliance.
description:
• Seamless burning and/or locking of liquidity pool tokens for a fraud-proof launch.
  • New LP burn alerts are integrated with SNEKbot and Snekx.
  • Metadata changes are integrated directly on the app without the need of third party assistance.
title: Advanced LP Token and Metadata Management Tool

acceptance_criteria:
Functionality of Customized Snapshot Tool

  • The snapshot tool must allow users to create customized snapshots with specific criteria and download the results as a CSV file.
  • This functionality should be tested with at least 100 test cases, achieving a 95% success rate in generating accurate snapshots.

Efficiency and Reliability of Airdrop Tool

  • The airdrop tool must enable users to plan and execute airdrops using a CSV file with a success rate of 95% or higher, validated through 100 test cases.
  • The tool should complete the airdrop process within a predefined time frame (e.g., within 10 minutes for 1,000 addresses).

User Feedback and Usability Testing

  • Collect feedback from at least 20 users who test the snapshot and airdrop tools. At least 90% of these users should report that the tools are intuitive and meet their expectations for ease of use and reliability.
description:
Development and Integration of Customized Snapshot Tool

  • Create and integrate a user-friendly tool that allows users to take customized snapshots of blockchain data.
  • This tool should enable users to select specific criteria for snapshots, such as address balances or transaction histories, and download the results in a CSV format without third-party assistance.

Development and Integration of Airdrop Tool

  • Develop and integrate a tool that enables users to plan and execute large-scale airdrops from a CSV file containing a list of addresses.
  • The tool should support automated distribution of tokens based on the provided list and criteria, ensuring efficient and error-free airdrops.
title: Snapshot and Airdrop Tool

acceptance_criteria:
Final Closeout Report and Video

  • The final closeout report and closeout video must be publicly available on the GitHub and to the Catalyst team.

Platform Performance

  • The platform must demonstrate high performance with specific metrics:
  • Token Minting Speed: Token minting operations must complete within 5-60 seconds in 95% of test cases.
  • Error-Free Operations: Token minting must be error-free in 98% of test cases across varied conditions, including high network traffic and low latency environments.
  • Security: The platform must pass a comprehensive security audit, confirming that there are no critical or high-severity vulnerabilities.
  • Scalability: The platform must handle at least 500-1,000 concurrent minting operations without significant performance degradation, with response times remaining under 10 seconds.

Platform Documentation

  • The following documentation must be completed and published on the Snekx GitHub (and potentially the website):
  • Legal review
  • Code review
  • Feature documentation
  • Terms of Service (TOS) implementation
  • The documentation should be detailed and provide clear instructions and information for developers and users.

acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:

  • Must submit a technical specification that details what features the Staking Basket bot will have.
  • This specification must also detail how it connects to the Cardano smart-contract.
description:
Staking Baskets are a Cardano smart-contract that allows you to delegate to over 100 SPOs at the same time. This stake distribution needs to be updated based on the Basket creators selection. There's no currently no automated process for this.

In this milestone we'll create a techincal specification that automates transactions that Basket creators need to submit every epoch for efficient Basket operation. This technical specification will detail what features the Staking Basket bot has, and how it connects to the Cardano smart-contract.
title: Staking Basket Bot Technical Spec

acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:

  • Video showing us using the update exchange rate endpoint, and the rebalancing endpoint. This will rebalance the stake in the Basket, and update the exchange rate.
  • We'll submit on-chain evidence of the exchange rate updating, and the stake rebalancing in the Basket.
  • We must submit some text to reviewers that shows how these inputs work, and how they are integrated with the smart-contract.
description:
The Staking Basket smart-contract allows users to deposit ADA into it for multi-delegation. Basket creators need to rebalance the ADA equally among all of the SPOs that are in the Basket.

In this milestone we'll create endpoints that allow someone to rebalance the stakepool. These endpoints will be created in TypeScript. After a user selects a predefined list of SPOs this endpoint can be called using that list to rebalance the stake in the Basket to the predefined list. As these are the two most important importants, we will label this the MVP of the Staking Basket bot.

Staking Baskets also need to have the exchange rate updated once per epoch. This exchange rate is already in the datums of the smart-contract. We're creating an endpoint in TypeScript to update the exchange rate.

To show these inputs working in action, we'll also output a video that shows them working. We'll also output some text to show what these endpoints do, and how they interact with the Basket.
title: Update Exchange Rate / Rebalance - Staking Basket Bot MVP

acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance:

  • Video showing us calling the endpoint to lock, and unlock the Basket. When calling this endpoint a transaction must be submitted, and the Basket must unlock, or lock.
  • Must submit on-chain evidence of locking, and unlocking the Basket that correlates with the video.
description:
Staking Baskets have a feature that allows them to lock the Basket. The time that it's locked is a predefined integer determined by the user. Locking is important before updating the exchange rate, or rebalancing the Basket. Locking beforehand makes sure no SPO loses staking rewards, and that the exchange rate is valid.

For this milestone we're going to create TypeScript endpoints for locking/unlocking Staking Baskets. These endpoints will eventually all be used for the bot in a later milestone.
title: Locking/Unlocking the Basket TypeScript Endpoint

acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance:

  • Must create a bot that automatically calls all endpoints created so far to update the exchange rate, lock the basket, and rebalance the stake within the Basket.
  • Must submit a video showing the bot working, and explain how it works with on-chain evidence shown in video.
  • Must submit on-chain evidence of the bot completing these tasks that corresponds with the video mentioned above.
description:
In this milestone we'll take all of the endpoints that we've created so far and write some code that calls them automatically.

Staking Baskets must rebalance once per epoch, and update the exchange rate once per epoch. To do both of these transactions the Basket needs to lock first. We're going to output code that does this automatically and get it running on Cardano's preview network with a real Staking Basket. The code will lock the Basket, then rebalance the ADA, and then update the exchange rate automatically.

Outputs:

  • Working Staking Basket bot code on Cardano's preview network.
  • Video showing the bot running with a real Staking Basket.
title: Staking Basket Bot Live

acceptance_criteria:
■ Research

We have already conducted research into transmitting information via television radio waves. In this research, we will investigate the technical feasibility of using broadcasting for authentication using the Cardano blockchain in an environment without the Internet, create a prototype, and conduct technical verification. (Design and implementation will be done in milestones 2 and 3) We would like to note that our team is primarily made up of broadcast engineers, and that we need to start by understanding how the Cardano blockchain works.

  • 1-a: The paper describes basic data processing flows, transactions, and metadata creation mechanisms.The paper must contain sources of information, images or illustrations and we will writte in English for its globalized understanding.
  • 1-b: We will demonstrate a thorough understanding of the Cardano blockchain and its compatibility with broadcast radio wave.
  • 2-a: Research on transactions and metadata creation on the Cardano platform
  • 2-b: Research on block headers and Merkle paths on the Cardano platform
  • 2-c: Research on data structures and entry encoding required for IPDC transmission
  • 3-a: Research on data structures and decoding for validation of received IPDC data
  • 3-b: Research on data structures required for validation

■ Prototype verification

  • 1: We will conduct technical verification of certificate issuance in Cardano and verify it in the Cardano system.
  • 2: We will conduct technical verification of certificate validation in Cardano.
description:
■ Research

  1. We will create a research paper in PDF format, describing the technical feasibility of using broadcast for authentication via the Cardano blockchain in an environment without Internet.
  2. Detailed technical report in PDF documenting the process and results of the verification of certificate issuance in Cardano.
  3. Detailed technical report in PDF documenting the process and results of the verification of certificate validation in Cardano.

■ Prototype verification

  1. Detailed technical report in PDF documenting the process and results of the verification of certificate issuance in Cardano.
  2. Detailed technical report in PDF documenting the process and results of the verification of certificate validation in Cardano.
title: Research and Prototype Verification

acceptance_criteria:
[1] Certificate issuing tool

This tool registers the certificate to issue certificates in places with an Internet connection. It also manages the information to be transmitted by IPDC (terrestrial) by acquiring transaction information at the time of registration.

[1-a] Function to register certificates

  • This Function is able to register and issue certificates.
  • This Function is able to manage and transmit information through IPDC(broadcast raidio wave).

[1-b] Function to acquire transaction information

  • This Function is able to acquire transaction information at the time of registration.

[2] Certificate IPDC transmission support tool

This tool provides an interface and necessary data processing for inputting data into the broadcast transmission system in order to transmit by IPDC (terrestrial).

[2-a] Function to build data for IPDC transmission

  • This Function is able to provide an interface and data processing necessary for input into the broadcast transmission system.
  • This Function is able to enable data transmission through IPDC (broadcast radio wave)
description:
[1] Certificate issuing tool

  • We will create a document for software processing specification. For example, It include that interface processing specification, define the blockchain transaction, the processing flow and authentication data.
  • Implement the program. (JavaScript + NodeJS is assumed)
  • Conduct implementation testing.
  • We will create a short video (2-3 minutes) demonstrating this tool.

[2] Certificate IPDC transmission support tool

  • We will create a document for software processing specification. For example, It include that interface processing specification, define the interface to the broadcast transmission, the processing flow, and transmission data.
  • Implement the program. (NodeJS is assumed)
  • Conduct implementation testing.
  • We will create a short video (2-3 minutes) demonstrating this tool.
title: Implementing a certificate issuing system

acceptance_criteria:

Assuming an environment without the Internet, this tool obtains information transmitted by IPDC (terrestrial broadcasting) from the broadcast and manages it appropriately. It also implements a validation process to verify certificates and a UI for displaying the results.

  • This tool allows you to manage certificate information received via IPDC (broadcast raidio wave).
  • This tool is able to performs the authentication and displays the resulting information.

1. RTO Pricing Model Specification:
  • Clarity and Completeness: The specification document must comprehensively outline the methodology, parameters, and assumptions used in the RTO pricing model. It should be detailed enough to guide the development of the calculator without requiring further clarification.
  • Alignment with Project Goals: The document should align with the overall goals of the tokenization platform as described in the original proposal, ensuring that the model supports the accurate and transparent pricing of assets.
  1. Working RTO Pricing Model Calculator:
  • Functionality: The calculator must accurately compute asset prices based on the inputs provided, adhering to the specifications outlined in the RTO Pricing Model Specification document. It should be user-friendly, with clear instructions and error-handling mechanisms.
  • Technical Validation: The calculator must undergo rigorous testing to ensure it functions correctly under various scenarios and input conditions. It must be free of critical bugs and operate efficiently within the tokenization platform.
  • Stakeholder Validation: The calculator must be demonstrated to and validated by key stakeholders, ensuring that it meets the project’s needs and expectations.
  1. Knowledge Centre:
  • Content Quality: The Knowledge Centre must contain comprehensive and well-organized documentation, guides, and educational materials that clearly explain the RTO Pricing Model and its applications within the tokenization platform.
  • Accessibility: The content must be easily accessible and understandable by a broad audience, including stakeholders, partners, and the Cardano community.
  • Positive Feedback: The Knowledge Centre must receive positive feedback from users, indicating that it is a valuable resource for understanding and using the RTO Pricing Model Calculator.
  1. Empowa Pay:
  • A demonstrable ability to reprice an asset based on data collected by Empowa Pay
  1. Sharing Outputs and Opportunities:
  • The working tool will be accompanied by a comprehensive report detailing its functionality.
  • We will organize 1 X workshop and 1 X webinar to demonstrate the model’s use, highlighting its potential for enhancing transparency and efficiency in real estate finance.
  • The underlying formulas will be made available in open-source repositories via a Google Sheet, fostering innovation, increasing transparency and encouraging developers to build on this foundation.
description:
1. RTO Pricing Model Specification:
  • What We Are Going to Do: Develop a detailed specification outlining the methodology, parameters, and assumptions used in the Rent-to-Own (RTO) pricing model. This document will cover the economic and financial principles applied, the tokenization framework, and the integration with the broader tokenization platform. This will be designed in partnership with the NSE to ensure the inputs include metrics important to institutional investors in Kenya and therefore the outputs are trusted.
  • How It Will Be Considered a Success: The specification is complete, and serves as a clear blueprint for the development of the RTO Pricing Model Calculator.
  • What Evidence We Will Provide That the Work Was Done: A finalized and approved RTO Pricing Model;
  1. Working RTO Pricing Model Calculator:
  • What We Are Going to Do: Develop a functional RTO Pricing Model Calculator based on the specified requirements completed in Milestone 1 and 2 and with the input of the NSE. This calculator will be the first working product of the tokenization platform, allowing for the accurate pricing of assets prior to tokenization. 
  • How It Will Be Considered a Success: The calculator is operational, accurately prices assets based on input parameters, and is tested and validated by internal teams and select stakeholders including the NSE.
  • What Evidence We Will Provide That the Work Was Done: Demonstrable, functional RTO Pricing Model Calculator, along with a user guide, test results, and stakeholder feedback.
  1. Knowledge Centre:
  • What We Are Going to Do: Create a Knowledge Centre that includes documentation, guides, and educational materials on the RTO Pricing Model and the broader tokenization platform. This will be aimed at stakeholders, partners, and the Cardano community to ensure transparency and understanding of the model and its applications.
  • How It Will Be Considered a Success: The Knowledge Centre is launched with comprehensive, accessible materials that are regularly updated. It receives positive feedback from users and helps in disseminating knowledge about the project.
  • What Evidence We Will Provide That the Work Was Done: The launch of the Knowledge Centre with all planned content available, user engagement analytics, and feedback reports.
  1. Empowa Pay:
  • Empowa Pay is a propriety platform built by Empowa and is actively being used by our developers to manage their rent-to-own contracts. By providing a solution for our developers to use we can more effectively track the performance of projects financed.
  • This additional source of near real-time data improves reporting to investors reducing their perceived risk and resulting in a cheaper cost of capital
  • The RTO calculator will be used to initially price projects, but the tool should also allow for the regular repricing of projects based on observed data in Empowa Pay this allows investors to more accurately determine whether a project tokens are trading at fair market value
  • This ability to regularly reprice an asset based on verified real-time data increases the attractiveness of using the NSE and Empowa platform for investing in affordable housing in Kenya


Sharing Outputs and Opportunities:

Upon completing the RTO Pricing Model Calculator milestone, we will share the specifications and a working version of the calculator with the Cardano community. This tool, which is designed to price real estate assets before tokenization, will be accompanied by a comprehensive report detailing its functionality. We will organize workshops and webinars to demonstrate the model’s use, highlighting its potential for enhancing transparency and efficiency in real estate finance. The underlying formulas will be made available in open-source repositories, fostering innovation, increasing transparency and encouraging developers to build on this foundation. This milestone will help position Cardano as a leading platform for financial solutions in emerging markets, driving further adoption and credibility.
title: Design and Development Phase 1 - RTO Pricing Model Calculator

acceptance_criteria:
1. The Liqwid Lending protocol (Liqwid) has listed the Gold token as a new market on its platform.


2. The DEX protocol has listed the Gold token as a new market on its platform.


3. Liquidity exists on the Gold market on Liqwid at Day 1. A liquidity provider has brought the liquidity at the start.

  • The liquidity amount will correspond at least to the minimum of 0.5% of the gold token minted and distributed to the market (= the market supply) and will be higher than $10’000.

 Note: We remind that providing liquidity is costly, and its optimum number is depending on the total amount of demand/supply and utility/market volatility.

Thus, the better the arbitrage is working, the less the amount of liquidity is required. The optimum amount will be evolving over time and setting a goal today with a fixed amount for a long duration is contra-productive.


4. Liquidity exists on the Gold market on DEX at Day 1. A liquidity provider has brought the liquidity at the start.

  • The liquidity amount will correspond at least to the minimum of 0.5% of the gold token minted and distributed to the market (= the market supply) and will be higher than $10’000.


5. Market maker activities are executing a trading strategy to ensure that the Gold TradFi price is the same / aligned with the on-chain price (on DEX). Some non-signification deviation may occurs, as it cannot be always 1:1 the same with zero deviation.


6. The findings from the audit report are resolved, regardless of their severity.
description:
1.Gold token is listed on Liqwid listing.

2. Gold token is listed on a DEX listing.


Information note about the liquidity:

Liquidity should be in place so that, on launch day (DAY 1), people can either buy the gold token from the DEX or borrow it from Liqwid.

For liquidity to exist at DAY 1, it means some users must have already completed the entire process (buying the gold, depositing physical gold in the safe place/ incl. in reserves, etc.) to mint the gold tokens (“Day 0” liquidity). acceptance_criteria:
There should be an interface that allows users to leverage our inheritance Dapp.

This front-end will have the following actions:

Create Vault -> A vault is a smart contract wallet to store the inheritance assets. Here, the users can set-up the initial configurations of the vault, such as the vault name, initial deadline, and vault icon.

Create Pocket -> A pocket is a storage unit within a vault where the vault owner deposit their tokens. After the vault deadline passes, a beneficiary can redeem the contents of the pocket if they possess the corresponding pocket key. A pocket is represented by a set of UTXOs, ie. the "parent" UTxO to hold metadata, and the "children" UTXOs that refer to its parent UTxO.

Update Vault -> This includes postponing the deadline as well as renaming the vault.

Update Pocket -> Right now this will just allow the users to rename their pockets.

Mint and Burn Vault Keys -> The ownership of a vault is determined by a token held in a user's wallet. By using Cardano's native token as access management, it's easy to transfer ownership instead of binding the ownership to certain identifier such as public key hash.

Mint and Burn Pocket Keys -> Similar to Vault Keys minting and burning, but Pocket Keys are meant to be held by the beneficiaries for them to be able to redeem from the corresponding pockets after the vault's deadline passes.

Deposit and Withdraw -> These actions enables the vault owner to deposit and withdraw assets to the pockets.

Vault Staking -> The vault can be staked. There are 4 actions: stake registration, pool delegation/redelegation, rewards withdrawal, and stake deregistration.

Pocket Deletion -> As the name suggest, this is to delete a pocket; by consuming the corresponding pocket UTxO as described in the pocket creation above.

description:
This milestone encompasses updating the specification of CIP-96 with respect to the following:

* Who has the right to submit a request for posting an audit artifact to the certification contract?

* How to guarantee that the audit artifact meets the expected standards necessary to generate the certification token (mainly to be used for on-chain upgrade verification)?

To achieve this milestone, the section "Certification issuers" in CIP-96 will be amended with a detailed description of the publication and review process for certification artifacts. Working out a suitable publication and artifact review process is part of the work required to complete this milestone.
title: Updating the specification of CIP-96

description:
This milestone encompasses updating the specification of CIP-96 with respect to the following:

  • How to accept new auditors and who are eligible to form the committee to review the request for posting audit artifacts ?
  • Update the certification contract datum to facilitate the implementation of a secure on-chain upgrade mechanism.

The outputs of this milestone will be presented as additional content on CIP-96. Section "Specification" will be amended as follows:

1. Insert a subsection "Auditors" that describes the on-chain mechanism used to identify eligible auditors (using a native token scheme) and the governance process that determines the set of auditors, as well as the activities required by an interested party to become an auditor.

2. Insert a subsection "On-chain protocol" that describes the way auditing-related information is recorded on the chain in a way that can be consumed by Plutus scripts, incl. examples. This description includes the tokens that are involved as well as datum and redeemer formats, and examples in pseudocode of scripts that use the proposed updating mechanism to securely upgrade to a new version.
title: Expanding CIP-96

description:
Updated SOM according to approved change request of Nov 13:

Advanced ZK protocol (build on “Semaphore”) + fully tested smart contracts (in Aiken)

Implement zk setup:

  • zk-SNARK Circuits: Create cryptographic circuits specifically for voting that verifies both voter eligibility and the correctness of their vote without revealing their identity or choices.
  • Proof Generation and Verification: Integrate semaphore library* for creating and verifying zk-SNARK proofs.

Implement Smart Contracts:

  • Voter Registration Contract: Registration of voters by verifying their zk-SNARK proofs of eligibility and issuing zk-based credentials for voting.
  • Voting & Tally Contract: Verifies zk-SNARK proofs that confirm a valid vote according to the voter’s credential and records the vote anonymously and aggregates votes and computes the final results.

Update documentation:

  • An updated system design that reflects the revised approach
  • A brief description of Semaphore along with its technical specification file


*Semaphore was an early POC for zk proofs on Cardano, which has a basic structure that is perfect for voting and whose trusted setup design significantly increases the security of the voting app.
title: Development of an advanced ZK protocol
